get.description: Handles the OIDC provider callback after user authentication. Validates the CSRF token, exchanges the authorization code for tokens, verifies the ID token, and issues a session JWT cookie.

302.description: Redirect to app after successful auth

502.description: Token exchange or ID token verification failed

get.description: Returns the OIDC issuer URL, client ID, and scopes so mobile clients only need the Phos server URL to self-configure authentication.
Initiates the OIDC login flow by redirecting the user to the configured identity provider. Stores PKCE and CSRF state in a signed cookie for the callback.
Clears the session cookie and redirects the user to the login page.

302.description: Redirect to login page after clearing session

get.description: Returns the current authenticated user's session claims (subject, name, email) from the session JWT cookie.

post.description: Accepts a currently-valid session (Authorization: Bearer header or session cookie) and issues a new session JWT with a fresh expiry. Expired or invalid sessions are rejected with 401 — this endpoint cannot resurrect an expired session. Cookie-authenticated callers also get the session cookie re-set.

post.summary: Exchange OIDC ID token for session JWT
post.description: Mobile clients perform the OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE flow directly with the identity provider, then send the resulting ID token here. Phos validates it against the provider's JWKS and returns a session JWT that can be used in the `Authorization: Bearer` header.

get.description: Metadata for the APK this server ships, so the Android app can offer an in-app update. Unauthenticated, like the /phos.apk download it describes. Always 200: a server with no bundled APK answers `available: false` with `version_code: 0`, which the client reads as "up to date".

200.description: The bundled APK, or `available: false` when there is none

post.summary: Describe a shot, and compile a prompt from it
post.description: Run a describe workflow against one shot and compile a prompt from what it says, together with the person names, EXIF date and place, and caption the library already holds. Answers immediately from the shot's cached description unless `refresh` is set. The compiled prompt is meant to be shown and edited before the costly stage is queued.

200.description: The description, or the run that will produce one

get.summary: The description a shot carries, and the prompt it compiles to
get.description: Poll for a describe run, or read the description a shot already carries. `intent`, `style` and `do_not` re-compile the prompt without describing the photograph again.

parameters.name: do_not
parameters.description: Constraints, one per line or separated by `;`.

200.description: Where the description has got to

post.description: Queue an image enhancement task using a ComfyUI workflow. Creates a background task that processes the shot's original file. A `vary` map queues one task per combination instead, and the response lists them in order.

400.description: Unrecognised source_mode, one this workflow cannot take, or an unusable sweep

get.description: Returns the workflow, text overrides and typed parameters used to generate each non-original file for a shot.
Check whether ComfyUI is configured and reachable. Returns the connection status and system info.
Every line in this library, with its stages and whether the chain still type-checks against the workflows' current contracts.

post.description: Store a chain of workflows. Rejected with a message naming the stage if any stage cannot consume what the one before it produces.

400.description: The chain does not fit together, or a stage is unusable

post.description: Read a line out of an exported bundle. Its workflows are created, or reused where an identical graph is already here, and its requirements are checked against what this ComfyUI has installed. A line whose nodes or models are missing is still imported; the response says what is missing. A name already in use is suffixed, never overwritten. Pass `dry_run=true` for the report alone.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description:
Check the bundle and report what it needs, writing nothing. Defaults to
`false`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name the imported line this rather than what the file calls it. A name
already in use is still suffixed rather than overwritten.

200.description: The imported line, and what it needs

400.description: The file is not a readable line export, or its chain does not fit together here

post.summary: Which workflows may go in one slot of a line
post.description: Send the line as it stands and the position being filled; every workflow comes back marked offered or refused. The verdict is `validate_chain` run over the line that each candidate would make, so a stage this offers can never be one that saving then refuses — and the refused ones come back too, each with the reason, so the editor can say what it is not offering and why.

get.summary: Lines somebody has already been running by hand
get.description: Sequences of workflows a person ran one at a time, over and over, on enough different shots to be a habit rather than an afternoon. Each comes back as a line ready to POST, with the settings that never changed pinned and the ones that did marked as asked-for.

post.summary: Check a line without saving it
post.description: The same check POST and PUT make, with nothing written. What the editor asks after a reorder, so a chain that no longer fits says so where it was dragged rather than after Save.

200.description: Whether it holds together, and why not

put.description: Replace a line's name, description and whole stage list. Refused while a run of this line is still in flight.

400.description: The chain does not fit together

409.description: A run of this line is still in flight
A run of this line is still in flight

post.description: Copy a line and everything its stages carry — workflows, prompts, parameters, sweeps, source modes, keep flags and exposed keys — under a new name. The default way to get a line, and the way to change one that a run is currently walking.

get.description: The line, its stages, the workflow graph behind every stage, and a manifest of the node classes and model files it needs — as one JSON document that can be imported into another library or another Phos install.

200.description: The line as a portable bundle

get.description: What ComfyUI says its installed node classes take: every input's name, type, default and range, and for an enum its contents — the checkpoints, samplers, schedulers and LoRAs installed on that server. Cached in memory for five minutes and re-read when ComfyUI comes back after being down; `refresh=true` re-reads it now. Always 200: a server that is unreachable or too old to have /object_info answers `available: false`, and the console falls back to plain text boxes.

parameters.name: classes
parameters.description:
Comma-separated class names to return. Omit for the whole catalogue,
which on a loaded install is several megabytes.

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description:
Read `/object_info` from ComfyUI now instead of serving the cached
copy. For after installing a model or a node pack.

get.description: The queue board: one row per run, newest first, with the stage it is on and how far along its line that is. The tasks underneath are reachable through GET /api/comfyui/runs/{id}.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Cursor: `next_cursor` from the previous page — `created_at|id` of its
last run. The id is the tie-breaker: a migrated backlog can put dozens
of runs on the same second, and a timestamp alone would skip the rest
of them.

post.summary: Start a production line against a shot
post.description: Open a run and queue its first stage. Each stage's output becomes the next stage's input as it completes. Refused if the line does not fit together, or if its first stage cannot read this shot.

400.description: The line does not fit, or does not fit this shot

get.summary: Get a run and its tasks
get.description: One run with every task under it, in stage order — the drill-down behind a board row.

post.description: Stop every task of a run that has not landed yet, interrupting on ComfyUI the one that is actually executing and dropping the rest from its queue.

get.summary: The takes a held run is waiting on
get.description: Every take of the stage this run is parked at, with what continuing from one of them will cost in tasks. Answers `null` for a run that is not holding anything.

post.summary: Give a verdict on a held run
post.description: `continue` proceeds with the takes named — more than one is ordinary, and each walks the rest of the line for itself. `regenerate` runs the held stage again with fresh seeds and nothing else changed, and the run holds again on the new takes. `cancel` abandons the run and removes its intermediates except where a stage says keep. Takes named in `reject` have their files removed from the library outright — that is the curation lane's `X`, and it is how a farm's disk stays habitable. `scope: batch` applies the same verdict to the rest of the batch; a rejection never travels with it.

400.description: The verdict names no takes, names a take this hold is not offering, or is not a verdict

409.description: This run is not holding anything for review

post.summary: Resume a run from the stage that failed
post.description: Re-queue every failed or cancelled task of a run, from the source file it was already given. Stages that already succeeded are not re-run.

400.description: Nothing in this run is waiting to be retried

get.summary: Every run waiting on a verdict
get.description: The curation lane: one page of held runs, oldest first, each with the takes it is holding, the file those takes were made from, the shot's current main file, and what continuing with one take will cost. Oldest first because this is a backlog somebody is draining, not a feed they are browsing.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Held runs per page. Default 24, capped at 100 — each row prices its own
continuation, so a page is real work.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Cursor: `created_at` of the last run from the previous page.

get.description: List ComfyUI enhancement tasks with optional status filtering and pagination.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Cursor: created_at value of the last item from the previous page

get.description: Retrieve details and current status of a specific enhancement task.

delete.description: Delete a completed or failed enhancement task record.

400.description: Task is not in failed or completed state

post.description: Stop an in-flight enhancement task: interrupt it on ComfyUI if it is the running prompt, drop it from ComfyUI's pending queue, and mark the task cancelled.
Retry a failed enhancement task. Resets it to pending status for reprocessing.

400.description: Task is not in failed state

get.description: List all imported ComfyUI enhancement workflows available for use. Each carries its stage contract: what it accepts (image / video / text / none), what it produces (image / video / text), which loader fills which slot, the prompt slots a person or a describe stage fills, and the typed parameters a line can set.

post.description: Import a ComfyUI workflow JSON for use as an enhancement pipeline.

delete.description: Delete an imported ComfyUI workflow by ID.

409.description: A production line still uses this workflow

put.description: Replace the corrections applied to a workflow's derived stage contract and return the contract that results. The heuristics are wrong on unusual graphs — a title that means something else, a saver Phos cannot classify, a prompt box wired somewhere unexpected — and this is how that is fixed without re-importing. Send an empty object to discard every correction and take the derivation as it stands.

get.description: Return the stored ComfyUI API-format graph for one workflow, alongside the inputs and outputs detected at import time.
List all prompt presets for a specific workflow.

post.description: Create a new prompt preset for a workflow with saved text overrides.

put.description: Update an existing prompt preset's name, text overrides, or sort order.

delete.description: Delete a prompt preset from a workflow.

post.description: Collapse overlapping face detections of the same face across the library, so reviewers do not have to delete them by hand. Two boxes assigned to different people are never merged, and shots already marked reviewed are left alone. Pass `dry_run=true` to get the count without deleting anything.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Report what would go without deleting anything. Defaults to `false`.

delete.description: Delete a face detection record. Cleans up orphaned people and recalculates shot assignments.

put.description: Reassign a face to a different person. Updates the shot's primary person if needed.

404.description: Face or target person not found

409.description: Face is on a machine-generated file and cannot join the person model

get.description: Get person assignment suggestions for a face based on embedding similarity to existing people.

200.description: List of person suggestions sorted by similarity

get.description: Retrieve the cropped JPEG thumbnail image for a detected face.

404.description: Face not found or source image missing

get.description: Download the original file content by file ID. Returns the raw bytes with the appropriate content type.

delete.description: Delete a non-original file from a shot. The original file cannot be deleted directly — delete the shot instead.

post.description: Manually add a face region to a file with a specified bounding box and person assignment.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: File ID to add a manual face to

409.description: File is machine-generated; faces on it are not accepted

get.description: Whether a file was generated, and the manifest recording how — the task and workflow that ran, the prompt overrides, the ComfyUI prompt id, the source file and the name the generator gave its output. Answers for any file: a photograph comes back with `synthetic: false` and no manifest.

put.description: The Takes lane's `1`–`5` keys. `null` clears the rating, which is a different answer from zero and is drawn differently. Any file may be rated, not only a generated one.
Mark a file as the original (primary) file for its shot, demoting the current original.

get.description: Retrieve a resized thumbnail or video preview for a file. Supports configurable dimensions via query parameters.

post.description: Finalize the import process by running a full library scan and reorganization on newly imported files.

get.description: How many uploaded files are still queued for or undergoing analysis, plus totals since the server started. Clients poll this after uploading to know when the library is fully indexed.

put.description: Upload a raw file for import. The file is written to the import staging area and queued for analysis, which runs in the background. Poll `/api/import/status` to see when it is done. Supports up to 1 GB files.

202.description: File stored and queued for analysis

get.description: Return detailed organization statistics including pending reviews, confirmed shots, unsorted shots, and unnamed people.
List all detected people with their name, face count, and a representative thumbnail face ID.

post.description: Create a new named person record that faces can be assigned to.
Merge two or more people into a single person. All faces from the source people are reassigned to the target person.

get.description: Retrieve all shots associated with a specific person, ordered by date.

delete.description: Delete a person and unassign all their faces. Shots will have their primary person recalculated.

get.description: Returns a complete person browse graph with all shots and their file variants in a single response. Designed for offline-first browsing clients. The reserved id `unsorted` returns the shots that belong to nobody yet.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Person ID, or `unsorted` for shots with no person

get.description: Retrieve all face thumbnail IDs belonging to a specific person.

post.description: Trigger a background filesystem reorganization that moves files into person-based folder structure.
Trigger a background library scan on the specified path to detect new or changed media files and run face detection.

get.description: List shots with optional filtering by person, date range, review status, and pagination. Returns brief shot metadata suitable for gallery views.

post.description: Confirm the person assignment for multiple shots at once, setting their review status to confirmed.
Reassign multiple shots to a different person in a single operation.
Merge two or more shots into a single shot. All files from the source shots are moved to the target shot.
Mark a pair of similar shots as intentionally separate so they are no longer suggested for merging.

get.description: Retrieve paginated groups of similar shots across the entire library for bulk deduplication review.
Retrieve full details for a single shot including all associated files, detected faces, and person assignments.

put.description: Update shot metadata such as the primary person assignment and review status.

delete.description: Delete a shot and all its associated files from disk and database. This action is irreversible.

get.description: Find shots visually similar to the given shot, grouped by the person they are assigned to. Uses perceptual hash comparison.

post.description: Split selected files out of a shot into a new separate shot. Useful when the scanner incorrectly groups unrelated files together.

get.description: Return aggregate library statistics including total shots, people, and files.
Return the current server version string.

Accepts.description:
What a stage consumes.

Four values rather than three, because "nothing" is a real answer: a
text-to-image graph begins a line instead of continuing one, and a line that
starts with it needs no upstream at all.

AddManualFacePayload.description:
POST /api/files/:id/faces - manually add a face bounding box.
The server computes the embedding from the given bbox coordinates.

Analysis.description:
The structured description a describe stage returns.

Structured on purpose: a paragraph is a thing to read, and this is a thing
to *use* — the fields are recombined per stage, the constraints become a
negative prompt, and the whole is cached and re-read by later runs.

do_not.description:
One constraint per entry. A model that answers with a single string
instead of a list is still answering; see [`StringOrList`].

AuthConfigResponse.description: Response for the auth config endpoint.

BatchReassignPayload.description: POST /api/shots/batch/reassign - batch set primary_person_id, assign new folder numbers, set confirmed.

synthetic.description: A workflow made this file, not a camera. The client says so.

BundleLine.description:
The line itself. Stage order is array order — there is no `stage_idx`,
because two sources of truth for one ordering is one too many.

BundleStage.description:
One step of a line, as it travels.

Field for field this is what line CRUD already takes, with one difference:
`workflow` is a key into this bundle's own `workflows` map rather than a
library id, because a library id is meaningless in the library it is being
carried to.

exposed.description:
Keys this stage leaves to whoever sends the line — the *exposed*
disposition. Optional, like everything else a hand-written template
would rather not say.

hold_for_review.description:
Whether this stage parks its run and asks which of its takes go on —
FR5c's hold point. Travels for the same reason again: a `×4 → hold →
upscale` line carried somewhere without the hold is a line that spends
four hours where the original spent one.

text_overrides.description:
Prompt bindings, plus the `role:<node_id>` directives the loader binder
reads.

workflow.description:
Which entry of `workflows` this stage runs. Any string: an export uses
the source library's workflow id, a hand-written template can use a
readable name.

contract.description:
The contract this workflow carried where it came from.

Optional, and re-derived on import against the *target* box's node
catalogue — only the `corrections` inside it survive verbatim, because a
correction is the one part of a contract that cannot be worked out
again. A hand-written template can leave it out entirely.

graph.description: The ComfyUI API-format graph, exactly as the library stores it.

ClientVersionResponse.description:
`GET /api/client/version` response — the bundled Android build.

Every field is non-nullable, so a generated client needs no null-handling at
all: "no APK bundled" is expressed by `available: false` with
`version_code: 0`, not by absent fields and not by an error status.

available.description:
Whether this server has an APK to offer at all.

`false` for a backend-only build, for local development, and whenever
the bundled metadata is unusable. A client that only compares version
codes does not need to read this — it exists so a "check for updates"
screen can say "this server does not ship an APK" instead of the
misleading "you are up to date".

download_path.description:
Server-relative path the APK downloads from, always populated so the
client never hardcodes it.

sha256.description:
Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the APK at `download_path`.

Empty when `available` is `false`. The client must verify the downloaded
bytes against this before handing them to the installer.

size_bytes.description:
Size of the APK in bytes, so a client can show download progress and
reject an obviously truncated response early. `0` when unavailable.

version_code.description:
`versionCode` of the bundled APK: the git commit count, monotonic on
master.

`0` when `available` is `false`. This is the only field an update
decision may be based on, and only as
`version_code > BuildConfig.VERSION_CODE` — never `!=`, which would
offer a downgrade after a rollback.

version_name.description:
`versionName` of the bundled APK — a tag (`1.2.3`) or `master+<sha>`.

Empty when `available` is `false`. Display only: version *names* are not
ordered and must never be compared.

CompiledPrompt.description: The two strings a generation stage takes.

ContractCorrections.description:
What a person said the derivation got wrong.

Kept beside the derived answer rather than replacing it, so the contract can
be re-derived — when ComfyUI comes back and the parameters can finally be
typed — without throwing the correction away.

params.description:
`"<node_id>.<field>"` → the setting it really is (one of [`ParamName`]),
or `null` for "that is not one of ours".

roles.description: `node_id` → the slot that loader really fills.

slots.description:
`"<node_id>.<field>"` → the prompt slot's name, or `null` for "that is
not a prompt".

CreatePersonPayload.description: Create a new person with a name

CreatedPerson.description:
The person that was just created.

Typed rather than a bare `serde_json::Value`, because the id is the whole
point of the call: "create this person and assign the shot to them" is one
user action, and a client that cannot read the id back has to re-list every
person and match on the name to find what it just made.

id.description: Generated person id, ready to be used as a `person_id` anywhere.

name.description: The name as stored — trimmed, which may differ from what was sent.

removed.description: Faces removed — or, for a dry run, faces that would be removed.

DescribePayload.description: What the caller wants described, and what for.

do_not.description:
What the run must not do. Reaches the model as a rule and the generation
stage as a negative prompt.

intent.description: The user's one line about what they are after.

refresh.description: Describe it again even though the shot already carries a description.

style.description: A style preset, in the preset's own words.

workflow_id.description:
Which describe workflow to run. Omit it and the first workflow whose
contract says `produces: text` is used.

DescribeResponse.description:
The description, the prompt it compiles to, and everything that went into
both — which is what makes the prompt correctable rather than magic.

oneOf.description: Its structured form, when the model produced one.

cached.description: Answered from `shots.analysis_json` rather than from a run.

facts.description: What Phos knew and the model could not see.

instruction.description: The instruction that was, or would be, sent into the describe workflow.

oneOf.description:
The two strings a generation stage takes. Editable: the dialog sends
whatever the person left in the box as an ordinary `text_overrides`
entry.

text.description: Exactly what the describe stage published, unedited.

DescribeState.description: Where the description for one shot has got to.

parameters.description:
Typed values for the workflow's non-text inputs, keyed
`"<node_id>.<field_name>"`: `{"3.seed": 4242, "3.cfg": 6.5,
"4.ckpt_name": "sd_xl_base_1.0.safetensors"}`. Each value keeps its own
JSON type, which is what `text_overrides` cannot do.

source_file_id.description: Optional: specific file to use as source. If omitted, the original file is used.

source_mode.description:
Which part of a video source to feed the workflow: `first_frame`,
`last_frame`, `at_time:<ms>`, `keyframe:<n>` or `whole_video`.

Omit it to let the workflow decide — a graph with a video loader takes
the whole clip, anything else takes the first frame. Ignored for stills.

vary.description:
Parameters to sweep rather than pin, keyed like `parameters`. Each entry
multiplies the number of tasks queued.

A value is one of three spellings: a count (`{"3.seed": 4}` — four runs
with four fresh seeds), an explicit list (`{"3.cfg": [4.0, 6.0, 8.0]}` —
three runs), or a `VarySpec` for the long form. Both of those together is
twelve runs; past 64 the request is refused.

Every value is resolved here, so each task is written with its own
complete parameter map and is replayable from its row.

Described as a free-form object rather than as a union of the three: the
generated Android client builds every model in the spec even though it
calls none of these endpoints, and an untagged union of a number, an
array and an object is not worth making it compile.

FaceSuggestion.description:
Get suggested persons for a face based on embedding similarity.

Computes cosine similarity on-the-fly between the target face and the
thumbnail face of every person, so results are always up-to-date even
for newly created persons.

synthetic.description:
Made by a machine rather than a camera. `GET /api/files/{id}/manifest`
says how.

FileManifestResponse.description: What a file says about where it came from.

oneOf.description:
How it was made. Absent for a photograph, and for a generated file that
predates provenance being recorded — a library can hold variants created
before anyone wrote down where they came from.

manifest_error.description:
Present when a stored manifest could not be read back. The raw text is
returned rather than dropped: unreadable provenance is still evidence.

manifest_raw.description: The stored manifest exactly as written, when it would not parse.

synthetic.description: Whether a machine made this picture rather than a camera.

IngestStatus.description:
What the queue is doing for one library, for the import UI to poll.

[`completed`] and [`failed`] count since the server started, not since the
current upload: the client knows how many files it sent, and the pair of
numbers it cares about — how many are still coming and whether any broke —
are both derivable from these without the server tracking upload sessions.

analyzing.description: Files being analyzed right now (0 or 1 — one worker per library).

failed.description: Files whose analysis failed since startup. They stay on disk.

Intent.description: What the person asked for, as opposed to what is in the photograph.

do_not.description:
What the run must not do. Reaches the model as a rule *and* the
generation stage as a negative prompt, because a model told not to do
something is not the same as a sampler steered away from it.

intent.description: One line: "a slow push-in as the light fades".

style.description: A style preset: "35mm film, muted palette".

LineBundle.description: A line, its stages, its workflows and what it needs installed.

exported_at.description: When it left, for a human reading the file. Never read by the importer.

requirements.description:
What this line needs installed, as computed where it was exported.

Documentation, not input: the importer recomputes it from the graphs in
this same file, so a stale or hand-edited manifest cannot make an import
report something untrue.

workflows.description: Every workflow the stages name, keyed by whatever they name it.

LineStagePayload.description:
One step of a line, as a client sends it.

Every field but `workflow_id` mirrors something a single-workflow enhance
already sends, and is stored and dispatched through exactly the same code —
which is why a stage of a line and an ad-hoc run cannot drift apart.

exposed.description:
Keys this stage deliberately leaves open — the *exposed* disposition.
Starting a run may supply values for exactly these, and only these.

hold_for_review.description:
Park the run after this stage and ask which of its takes go on. Refused
on the last stage, whose output is the product.

keep_output.description:
Keep this stage's output once the run completes. The last stage's output
is the product and is kept regardless, and so are the takes of a stage
that holds for review.

parameters.description:
Typed values for this stage's non-text inputs, keyed
`"<node_id>.<field_name>"`.

source_mode.description:
Which part of an upstream video this stage consumes: `first_frame`,
`last_frame`, `at_time:<ms>`, `keyframe:<n>` or `whole_video`. Omit it
to let the graph decide.

text_overrides.description:
Prompt bindings, plus the `role:<node_id>` directives the loader binder
reads.

vary.description:
Parameters to sweep rather than pin. Expanded once per continuation, so
a count of 4 here means four takes and four independent runners through
every stage after this one.

MediaType.description:
What flows from one stage to the next.

Three, and `text` is one of them: a text-producing stage writes no file at
all, so it is not a degenerate image.

MergePeoplePayload.description: Merge two people: move all faces from source to target, then delete source

MergeShotsPayload.description: POST /api/shots/merge - move all files from source to target shot. Delete source.

ModelRef.description:
One weights file a graph names, and where it names it.

The node class and field are carried because "sd_xl.safetensors is missing"
is not actionable and "CheckpointLoaderSimple wants sd_xl.safetensors in
ckpt_name" is: it says which of ComfyUI's model directories to put it in.

OrganizeStatsResponse.description: Return detailed organize stats about the library

ParamName.description:
A knob a line can set on any stage without knowing which node holds it.

A closed vocabulary on purpose. The exhaustive per-node control surface is
[`detect_inputs`]' job; a contract names only the handful of settings that
mean the same thing on every stage, so a line can say "seed 42" once.

PersonFaceBrief.description: Get up to 12 face IDs with thumbnail URLs for a person

PersonMeta.description:
Browse a person: returns person metadata + all shots + all files per shot.
Solves the N+1 problem for the mobile client.

parameters.description:
The preset's typed values, keyed like a task's `parameters`. A preset
that can pin a prompt but not a seed or a step count is half a preset.

ProvenanceManifest.description: How a generated file came to exist.

comfyui_prompt_id.description:
ComfyUI's own id for the run, which is how its history can still be
matched up if the server keeps it.

compiled_prompt.description: The prompt as submitted, after every override was applied.

generated_at.description: When Phos brought the file into the library, UTC, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

line_id.description: The generation line this file belongs to.

output_filename.description:
The name ComfyUI gave the output, before Phos renamed it into the
library — the last thread back to the run that made it.

parameters.description:
The typed values this run ran with, `"<node_id>.<field_name>"` → value,
exactly as the task row carried them.

This is what makes a fanned-out run reproducible one file at a time: four
takes of the same prompt differ only here, and without it their manifests
are indistinguishable.

seed.description:
The seed the sampler actually ran with, lifted out of [`Self::parameters`]
because it is the value asked for most often. A graph with two samplers
has two seeds; this is the first in key order, and the map beside it is
the complete answer.

source_file_id.description: The library file the run was given to work from, when there was one.

stage_index.description: Position of this run in a multi-stage line, zero-based.

text_overrides.description: The text the user put into the workflow, node id → prompt.

version.description: Which shape of this record was written. See [`MANIFEST_VERSION`].

additionalProperties.description:
Anything a newer Phos wrote that this one has no field for. Kept so a
round trip through an older binary does not quietly drop provenance.

Flattened, so it has no name of its own in the JSON and nothing to
publish in the schema — a client generated from an older spec simply
does not see the newer keys, which is the point.

rating.description:
One to five, or `null` to clear it. Out of range is clamped, not
refused: the lane cannot produce a six, so one is a caller's bug and
losing somebody's keystroke over it helps nobody.

ReassignFacePayload.description: Reassign a face to a different person

Requirements.description: What a line needs installed on the ComfyUI that will run it.

models.description: Every weights file the graphs name, sorted.

node_classes.description: Every distinct `class_type` in the line's graphs, sorted.

RequirementsReport.description:
What the catalogue said, and what is missing.

Never a refusal on its own: an import goes through with things missing, so a
line can be filed on the box that stores the library and run on the box that
has the GPU. The report is what the person acts on.

checked.description: False when there was no catalogue to check against.

missing_models.description: Weights files this ComfyUI's own enum of installed files does not list.

missing_nodes.description: Node classes this ComfyUI does not have. Naming them is the whole point.

unverified_models.description: Weights files that could be neither confirmed nor denied.

access_key.description: The S3 access key id (OIDC sub in multi-user mode, "phos" in single-user).

bucket.description: The fixed bucket name the library is exposed as.

endpoint.description: External endpoint URL override (PHOS_S3_PUBLIC_URL), if configured.

secret_key.description:
The secret key. Stored in plaintext server-side because SigV4 signing
requires the real secret; only returned to the authenticated owner.

SessionClaims.description: JWT claims for the user session cookie.

synthetic.description:
The shot's main file was made by a machine. The card says so, because
the picture itself cannot.

ShotFacts.description:
What the library already holds about one photograph.

Every field is what a vision model cannot get from the pixels: who these
people are, when this was, where it was, and the caption search already
matches on. Read from the database by [`shot_facts`]; a pure value here so
the wording can be exercised without one.

caption.description:
The Florence-2 library caption from `shots.description`. Read as one
input among several: it is what search matches on, and it is emphatically
not the prompt.

people.description:
The named people clustered onto this shot, primary person first.
Unnamed clusters are left out: "person 4f2a" helps nobody.

place.description:
EXIF coordinates. Phos has no geocoder, so this is degrees and says so
— a model that recognises the place from the pixels can still use them
as corroboration.

taken_at.description: The EXIF capture time, as stored (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`).

SourceRole.description:
Which slot of a multi-input workflow a source fills.

Three is enough for every graph worth running: the frame a clip starts on,
the frame it ends on, and a picture that is neither (a style or pose
reference).

SplitShotPayload.description:
POST /api/shots/:id/split - create new shot from specified files.
New shot inherits primary person from faces. Both shots get review_status = 'pending'.

StageOptionsPayload.description:
The draft being edited, and where in it a stage is going.

The whole draft rather than the two types either side of the slot, because
whether a stage fits is a question about the *line*: a stage that makes no
file is transparent to what flows past it, so the join above position 3 is
not necessarily what stage 2 produced. Sending the line and letting
`validate_chain` answer is the only shape that cannot fall behind that rule.

mode.description:
`insert` (the default) pushes whatever is at `at` down; `replace` puts
the candidate in its place.

stages.description:
The workflow ids of the line as it stands, in order. Empty for a line
with no stages yet.

StartRunPayload.description:
What starts a run.

FR7 adds a query in place of `shot_id` and a cursor beside it; the handler
is already written around "which shots does this ask for", so that is a new
field rather than a new endpoint.

stage_values.description:
Values for the keys each stage left open, keyed by stage index as a
string. A key a stage did not expose is refused by name rather than
ignored.

StatsResponse.description: Return aggregate stats about the library

TokenResponse.description: Response containing a Phos session JWT.

UpdateShotPayload.description:
PUT /api/shots/:id - update primary_person_id and/or review_status.
When primary_person changes, assign new folder_number (MAX+1 for that person).

VaryMode.description: How a swept parameter picks its values when no explicit list is given.

VarySpec.description: The long form of a sweep, for when it needs to say how.

count.description: Or: how many values to generate. Ignored when `values` is given.

min.description:
The range a generated value stays inside — the node's own bounds, when
the catalogue knew them.

values.description:
Run exactly these values, in this order.

Any scalar JSON value: `[4.0, 6.0, 8.0]` for a cfg,
`["sd15.safetensors", "sdxl.safetensors"]` for a checkpoint. Declared
as unconstrained values, not objects — `Vec<Object>` would make a
generated client refuse every valid list.

VerdictPayload.description: What a person said about a held run.

keep.description:
The takes that go on, by task id. Required for `continue` and ignored by
the other two, which are about the hold rather than about a selection.

note.description: Why, in the reviewer's own words. Kept with the verdict.

reject.description:
The takes whose **bytes go**, by task id — the curation lane's `X`.

Deleting, not passing over: a take nobody named is disposed of by its
stage's `keep_output` policy, which is the line author's decision, while
a rejected one goes regardless, which is the reviewer's. Generated video
is enormous and a farm fills a disk in days, so this is the key that
keeps the library habitable.

Never carried to another run by `scope`, whatever it says. Deleting
bytes is something you do to pictures you have looked at.

scope.description:
How far this verdict reaches: `run` (the default) or `batch`.

`batch` applies the same verdict to every other run of the same FR7
batch held at the same stage of the same line. `continue` resolves there
to *all* of that run's waiting takes, because task ids are per run and
the selection made here does not exist there.

username.description: The WebDAV username (OIDC sub in multi-user mode, "phos" in single-user).

session_cookie.description: Session JWT set as HttpOnly cookie (phos_session) after OIDC login
